title: Looking after the new bassist on the road
summary: Thomas remembers Lamar Wright sending ahead for rooms and persuading a landlady in the Midwest to take in Hinton.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I always had compassion for new guys that came in the band. And I heard you play, because we brought the book out on you, and you played all them darn things, and you was a new man, and you didn't know the road like the rest of us... We'd been out there, and been in that town two or three times. And Lamar Wright, I relied on him to say where I was living. I didn't worry about it.

So he wrote ahead of time... He had where we stayed, he had dinner and everything ready for us. And when you showed up and didn't have no place to stay, we got to talking to the lady, said, 'Miss, don't you have a room you can give this boy?' Because we didn't want you to be out there running around and trying to find a room...

The (?) had turned me down. I'll tell you what town it was in. It was Des Moines or Davenport or Moline, one of those three towns. That's where it was. I shall never forget it if I live to be a thousand.

And I was happy afterwards, because I really didn't know how good a musician you were. But I knew that you was a strange guy coming in the band, and we had to look out for you. Well, for me to get into it with the straw bosses, the first trumpet player and the assistant conductor was like (?) from heaven.
